title: Pleasing God · Chapter 5: The Holy Spirit: The Power of the God Pleaser
speaker: Joshua Heward-Mills
text:
Chapter 5

# The Holy Spirit: The Power of the God Pleaser

And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

Matthew 3:16-17 (KJV)

Jesus is the perfect example of a life pleasing to God. At His baptism, the Holy Spirit descended upon Him, and the Father declared His pleasure in Him. We need to pay attention to that connection. The power to live a life pleasing to God comes from the Holy Spirit.

Even David, whom we readily describe as a man who obeyed God, had a serious failure recorded against him in the matter of Uriah.

Because David did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

1 Kings 15:5 (KJV)

We must not make another human being our final standard. Jesus is the One to whom we look.

Much of His early life is not laid out for us in public detail. At twelve, He was in the temple, listening and asking questions. Then there are years about which the record says comparatively little.

And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.

Luke 2:46 (KJV)

We do not need everybody to know everything we are doing before God. Quietness is a spiritual quality worth learning.

And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;

1 Thessalonians 4:11 (KJV)

Another version says to make it your ambition to lead a quiet life:

and to make it your ambition to lead a quiet life and attend to your own business and work with your hands, just as we commanded you,

1 Thessalonians 4:11 (NASB 1995)

There is a difference between living well and making a public display of living well. A person can put so much effort into what is visible that the inward life is neglected. Even in ministry, attention continually directed outside can leave the work entrusted to us at home unattended. Learn to attend to the life God has actually given you.

A spiritual person is one who is completely dominated by the Holy Spirit. His thoughts, his will, his intentions, his mind, his actions are determined and restricted by the Holy Spirit. The more of your life that is controlled and determined by the Holy Spirit, the more spiritual you are.

The Holy Spirit is a person. He's not a thing. He's not smoke or a force or a wind. The single greatest revelation of my whole life was that the Holy Spirit is a person. If you ask me to point out one thing that completely changed my life, it's when I found out that the Holy Spirit is a person.

What should you do to be pleasing to God? It's very simple. Be like Jesus. That's what makes Him happy. Inasmuch as you are like Jesus, that is how much you please God. You just need to compare how you are to how Jesus was.

During a teaching session, I asked two men to stand in front of the congregation. One represented Jesus; the other represented a believer wanting to please God. If I pointed to the first man and said, “This is what pleases me; become like him,” the second man would have a clear reference. He could compare himself with the model rather than inventing his own standard.

The illustration is simple, but the standard is high. How can a human being become like Jesus?

But we Christians have no veil over our faces; we can be mirrors that brightly reflect the glory of the Lord. And as the Spirit of the Lord works within us, we become more and more like him.

2 Corinthians 3:18 (TLB)

As the Spirit of the Lord works within us, we become more and more like Him. What's the location of the work? Within. The Holy Spirit is going to work inside you. He's going to change you from the inside out to become more and more like Jesus. That's the greatest work of the Holy Spirit.

# 1. He works in you to desire what pleases God.

Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling. For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure.

Philippians 2:12-13 (KJV)

Many Christians know the instruction to work out their salvation with fear and trembling, but they stop before the explanation in the next verse. God is at work in us, both to will and to do His good pleasure.

Work out your salvation. You're saved—now show it. Live like you're saved. Talk like you're saved. But the working out is an outward effect of the indwelling work of the Spirit within you. Without the work of the Spirit inside a believer, I tell you, he's saved but not changed. It's one thing to be saved and another thing to be Christlike.

A lot of people were proud before they were saved, and after they're saved they're still proud. But they speak Christianese. They say, “Praise the Lord!”—but proud. Saved, but disobedient.

What was Jesus like? He lived in dependence on the Father.

I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.

John 5:30 (KJV)

Even when asked about places of honour, He did not treat them as something He could independently distribute.

And he said unto her, What wilt thou? She saith unto him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom. But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able. And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.

Matthew 20:21-23 (KJV)

Christlikeness reaches into relationships, decisions, and the things we assume are ours to arrange.

A lot of Christians have changed some version of the outside. Even Satan is changed into an angel of light. It's a presentation he has. Now you say, “Praise the Lord. God bless you.” But you are still the same person you were, full of envy, lust, jealousy, self-will, unkindness, wickedness, unforgiveness. We need the fruit of His work.

And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

2 Corinthians 11:14-15 (KJV)

We do not want that kind of change—a presentation of righteousness while envy, lust, wickedness, unforgiveness, and self-will remain untouched within us. We want the fruit of the Spirit.

But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

Galatians 5:22-23 (KJV)

What works inwardly eventually becomes visible. A serious condition can exist inside a body before its effects are obvious outside. In the same way, an inward spiritual work produces an outward result. Trying to reverse the order by managing the appearance alone leaves us pretending.

He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.

Acts 19:2 (KJV)

The question about receiving the Holy Spirit after believing should make us take His work seriously. I believed before I understood much about His inward operation. We need more than familiarity with Christian language; we need Him.

Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:

Philippians 1:6 (KJV)

He begins a good work in us and continues it. What does He do? Philippians 2:13 names two things: He works in us to will, and He works in us to do. First there is desire; then there is the power to act. Look at it in the New Living Translation:

For God is working in you, giving you the desire and the power to do what pleases him.

Philippians 2:13 (NLT)

Look at it in The Living Bible:

For God is at work within you, helping you want to obey him, and then helping you do what he wants.

Philippians 2:13 (TLB)

That’s why I like The Living Bible: it says, “and then helping you”. The doing always comes second. Let’s start with the will.

This is what we know traditionally: this is your will, this is God's will. Then you say, “Not my will, but Your will be done.” I can't say it doesn't exist. But God's real work in you is when you say, “My will is His will.” I'm not fighting between what I want and what God wants. I want what God wants.

The call to full-time ministry is not a loss of understanding of life. It's not a lack of understanding of financial realities, a future, and a destiny. No, it's the work of the Spirit inside a person. He has no desire for what you desire. He has a new desire within him.

The work reaches into the soul—our thoughts, affections, and desires. A new vocabulary is not enough. We need an inward transformation.

I was speaking to a woman who was considering marriage. I explained that I would approach the matter by asking to know what God wanted, with a heart already eager to receive His will. Instead of merely asking Him to bring somebody who fits every independent desire, I want Him to work on the desire itself.

I once strongly wanted a career in law. I read legal novels, enjoyed courtroom dramas, loved the subject, and wanted to build a law firm. I loved order and the way an argument could be followed line by line. I even remember becoming so enthusiastic in a constitutional law lecture that I responded as though I were in a sermon.

But the Holy Spirit worked in me. It did not finally feel like being forced to accept something I hated. I began to want to serve God with my whole life.

I had choices about where to live and work. Staying in Ghana was not the only opportunity legally open to me. Nor did I leave employment because I did not understand its benefits. I had earned well. I knew what it was to buy things without carefully planning every expense, to travel, and to enjoy the comfort that money could provide.

Once, while I was at work, my pastor told me he was travelling to minister in another country. I realised that I had my passport with me. I took a taxi to the airport, bought a ticket, and joined him without even going home to pack. I could buy what I needed when I arrived. That was the kind of freedom I was accustomed to.

When I was preparing to leave my job, there were further opportunities, including an offer connected with work in Kuwait. My employer also proposed increasing my salary. But I could not wait to leave and serve God. There was no comparable financial arrangement waiting for me in ministry. For a time I received no salary, and the salary I later received was a small fraction of what I had earned.

I couldn't wait to leave. I was so excited. “I just want to serve You, God.” It sounded so attractive to me—to work for God with all my life. I knew the difficulties more than most. I knew what it meant. But I wanted to spend my whole life looking after His people. It's not that I don't know what's nice or comfortable. Your desires change when the Spirit works within you.

And I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit in you. I will take out your stony, stubborn heart and give you a tender, responsive heart. And I will put my Spirit in you so that you will follow my decrees and be careful to obey my regulations.

Ezekiel 36:26-27 (NLT)

The Living Bible says:

And I will put my Spirit within you so that you will obey my laws and do whatever I command.

Ezekiel 36:27 (TLB)

The Good News Translation says:

I will put my spirit in you and will see to it that you follow my laws and keep all the commands I have given you.

Ezekiel 36:27 (GNT)

And the New International Reader’s Version says:

I will put my Spirit in you. I will make you want to obey my rules. I want you to be careful to keep my laws.

Ezekiel 36:27 (NIrV)

“I will make you want.” The work is not just to make you do. That’s part two. He will make you want.

God speaks about taking away a stony heart and giving a heart of flesh. He puts His Spirit within His people and causes them to walk in His statutes. A tender, responsive heart is different from a stubborn heart that is always fighting to keep its own way.

Do not make Gethsemane the permanent address of your soul, as though the only possible spiritual experience is an endless struggle against what God wants. The Holy Spirit can make you delight in His will.

Jesus lived in dependence on the Father. What He did and taught was not an independent project.

Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.

John 5:19 (KJV)

Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.

John 7:16 (KJV)

The agony of Gethsemane was real, and Scripture speaks seriously about His prayers, tears, suffering, and obedience.

Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared; Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;

Hebrews 5:7-8 (KJV)

We must not dismiss the cost of obedience. But neither should we deny the Spirit's power to change what we desire. Moses' choice to identify with God's people rather than the pleasures of Egypt also shows that something greater can govern the heart.

By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.

Hebrews 11:24-26 (KJV)

Watch out when you have new desires, because you're about to do it. Why do you want to come to church? Why do you want to hear the Word? Why do you like verses? Why is it attractive to you? The word shepherd is attractive to me. It's my calling. Why? Because it's God working in you, giving you the desire, and then the power to do.

It is God working within you. The desire is part of the work He has begun.

# 2. He works in you to do what pleases God.

The same Spirit who gives the desire also gives power to do. He does not begin a work merely to leave it as an unfulfilled longing.

Second Corinthians 3:18 says that we are changed from glory to glory. The New American Standard Bible puts it this way:

But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as from the Lord, the Spirit.

2 Corinthians 3:18 (NASB 1995)

You don't go from zero to a hundred in a day with God. God does everything step by step. Your desires won't all change by tomorrow. It changes slowly. We are changed from glory to glory—one step at a time.

Jacob's vision at Bethel gives us an image of movement by a ladder—ascending and descending. Think of steps rather than imagining that every level of maturity must arrive at once.

And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.

Genesis 28:12 (KJV)

There are spiritual exercises through which we make ourselves available to the Spirit's work.

But refuse profane and old wives’ fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness. For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.

1 Timothy 4:7-8 (KJV)

Godliness is an exercise. Spirituality is like going to the gym. It doesn't happen in a day. You need to discipline yourself and lift weights. The Spirit will dominate you through spiritual disciplines. Going to church. Prayer. Reading your Bible. This is how the Spirit slowly starts to dominate your life and change your will.

Coming to hear the Word is a discipline. Jesus went to John at the Jordan. Prayer is a discipline. Luke's account connects His baptism with prayer.

Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened, And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

Luke 3:21-22 (KJV)

Learn to surrender yourself to God throughout the day. When I arrive at the office, I want Him to lead the hours and minutes ahead. Before preaching, I ask for His help. Prayer is not simply a long event at one end of the day; it is part of a life that keeps yielding to Him.

Reading the Word is another discipline. Jesus came up out of the baptismal water. I also use that picture to ask a spiritual question: are we coming out of the Word? Have we spent time in it before entering the day's other activities? Scripture itself associates cleansing with water and the Word.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word,

Ephesians 5:25-26 (KJV)

The baptismal water in Matthew remains actual water; the application is that we need the discipline of the Word in our lives. We cannot continually avoid the things through which God works and then be surprised that our desires remain unchanged.

Submission also requires discipline. Jesus did not treat Himself as above the act of coming for baptism. We too must be willing to take our place, receive ministry, and accept the inconvenience that learning may involve.

But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.

1 Corinthians 9:27 (KJV)

Discipline concerns the body as well as the mind. Can you wake a little earlier to pray? Can you read a verse or two faithfully? Can you arrive for a service rather than constantly giving God whatever time is left over?

You can't stop certain things or start certain things, but you can discipline yourself slowly, every day. Allow the Spirit to work on you. It's really that simple. Exercise yourself unto godliness.

Make me to go in the path of thy commandments; for therein do I delight.

Psalm 119:35 (KJV)

There is a delight in God's commandments that we should seek. His work is not merely to leave us permanently dragged towards something we hate.

Do not mistake a decision for a completed exercise. Somebody can go to the gym, feel sore the next day, and imagine that strength must already have arrived. Yet the repeated work still has to be done. Spiritual discipline is also something to continue.

God's Word speaks of a heart of stone. How is stone broken?

Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?

Jeremiah 23:29 (KJV)

A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.

Ezekiel 36:26 (KJV)

The Word is a hammer. It chips away at what is hard within us.

When we altered the church building, there was an old concrete beam that had to be removed. The concrete was extremely strong. It did not disappear through one touch. Day after day, a little more was chiselled away.

Is this your stubborn heart? Every day you miss, a little more of your heart has been left. You had a chance to chisel. Take the chisel, take the hammer, break a small piece off, then go to work. Exercise. He will dominate your life. That's what brings the change.

My love for prayer did not begin as a natural enjoyment of long meetings. I used to dislike prayer. I could think that I had prayed for an hour and discover that only a few minutes had passed. Group prayer was even harder for me.

But I began attending church and listening to messages. After a time, I felt a desire to wake and pray on my own. The thing that had seemed impossible became something I wanted to do. Later I found myself praying for long periods alone, without anybody knowing or supervising me.

That was not merely a victory of my original temperament. The Spirit had worked on the person who used to hate prayer.

Paul also spoke about a life that had been very different before God's mercy reached him.

Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.

1 Timothy 1:13 (KJV)

His calling was followed by a life in which he was being dealt with and taught. He spoke of going into Arabia and returning to Damascus.

But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace, To reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the heathen; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.

Galatians 1:15-17 (KJV)

Let God have the time and space to work on you. Jesus taught daily, and the people came to hear Him.

And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him, And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.

Luke 19:47-48 (KJV)

Sometimes I give people work in church partly because that work brings them into the atmosphere of worship and the Word more often. They come for a full service rather than half of one. Later they attend another meeting. While serving, they hear things that begin to change them.

People operating the scripture projection keep encountering Bible passages. Worshippers at rehearsal hear words and scriptures they would otherwise have missed. These may seem small things, but repeated exposure matters. A little more of the hard heart is being addressed.

The histories of believers who suffered for Christ show how deeply desires can change. Some were willing to face death rather than renounce Him. Something greater than comfort, safety, and worldly gain had taken hold of their hearts.

We were made to love God. The love of Christ reaches beyond what we can fully understand.

And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God.

Ephesians 3:19 (KJV)

There is a satisfaction in Him greater than the world's substitutes. Be alone with Him. Give yourself to the exercises through which the Holy Spirit works. Let Him change you from within, step by step.

The Holy Spirit is the power that makes you please God. He changes your heart. It's God working in you, giving you the desire and the power to do what pleases Him. Allow the Spirit to work in you. Open your Bible. Pray. Come to hear the Word. It doesn't happen in a day. Slowly He changes you, from glory to glory.
